subject: CFA script reporting two different sets of results after running SEM

messages.author: e76612751d0fd653
messages.subject: CFA script reporting two different sets of results after running SEM
parts:
I have been playing around with some CFA and SEM models. The first CFA model I ran using the script:

PTmod2 <- ('OVPSS =~ w1ovpss1 + w1ovpss2 + w1ovpss3
          OVSUB =~ w1ovsub1 + w1ovsub2 + w1ovsub3_r
          OEPSS =~ w1oepss1 + w1oepss2 + w1oepss3
          OESUB =~ w1oesub1 + w1oesub2 + w1oesub3
          PSC =~ w1psc1_r + w1psc2 + w1psc3
          OA =~ w1oa1 + w1oa2 + w1oa3
          OV =~ w1ov1 + w1ov2 + w1ov3
          RA =~ w1ra1 + w1ra2 + w1ra3
          RV =~ w1rv1 + w1rv2 + w1rv3
          FA =~ w1parea1 + w1parea2 + w1parea3
          FV =~ w1pvrev1 + w1pvrev2 + w1pvrev3')

PTFIT2 = cfa(PTmod2, data=DATA, estimator="ML", std.lv=TRUE) 
summary(PTFIT2, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized=TRUE)

It returned the errors: 

Warning message:
In lavaan::lavaan(model = PTmod2, data = PapaTodd, std.lv = TRUE,  :
  lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate.

This error made sense given the nature of the data. Later on in my project I ran the SEM script:

PTsem2 <- ('OVPSS =~ w1ovpss1 + w1ovpss2 + w1ovpss3
          OVSUB =~ w1ovsub1 + w1ovsub2 + w1ovsub3_r
          OEPSS =~ w1oepss1 + w1oepss2 + w1oepss3
          OESUB =~ w1oesub1 + w1oesub2 + w1oesub3
          PSC =~ w1psc1_r + w1psc2 + w1psc3
          OA =~ w1oa1 + w1oa2 + w1oa3
          OV =~ w1ov1 + w1ov2 + w1ov3
          RA =~ w1ra1 + w1ra2 + w1ra3
          RV =~ w1rv1 + w1rv2 + w1rv3
          PA =~ w1pa1 + w1pa2 + w1pa3
          PV =~ w1pv1 + w1pv2 + w1pv3
          REA =~ w1rea1 + w1rea2 + w1rea3
          REV =~ w1rev1 + w1rev2 + w1rev3
          OVPSS ~ OA + OV + RA + RV + PA + PV + REA + REV
          OVSUB ~ OA + OV + RA + RV + PA + PV + REA + REV
          OEPSS ~ OA + OV + RA + RV + PA + PV + REA + REV
          OESUB ~ OA + OV + RA + RV + PA + PV + REA + REV
          PSC ~ OA + OV + RA + RV + PA + PV + REA + REV')

PTSEMFIT2 <- sem(PTsem2, data = PapaTodd, estimator="ML", std.lv=TRUE)
summary(PTSEMFIT2, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized=TRUE)

It returned the errors:

Warning messages:
1: In lav_samplestats_from_data(lavdata = lavdata, missing = lavoptions$missing,  :
  lavaan WARNING: sample covariance can not be inverted
2: In lavaan::lavaan(model = PTsem2, data = PapaTodd, std.lv = TRUE,  :
  lavaan WARNING: model has NOT converged!

AND

Warning messages:
1: In .local(object, ...) :
  lavaan WARNING: fit measures not available if model did not converge


2: In sqrt(ETA2) : NaNs produced

After running that SEM, if I return to the first CFA and rerun it, the exact same script, I get the errors:

Warning messages:
1: In lav_samplestats_from_data(lavdata = lavdata, missing = lavoptions$missing,  :
  lavaan WARNING: sample covariance can not be inverted
2: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
  lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

3: In lavaan::lavaan(model = PTmod2, data = PapaTodd, std.lv = TRUE,  :
  lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate.

I am running literally the exact same script for that CFA and it is now not working. Did running that SEM alter my data in some way?

Thanks!

I am running literally the exact same script for that CFA and it is now not working. Did running that SEM alter my data in some way?

Running an SEM on the data doesn't change the data.frame you analyze, but some other change might have been made between the original and later analyses.  Since you ran the same script "later", I'm guessing that lavaan was updated in between the original run and the latest run.  Yves tries to make messages as informative as possible, so the update may have included a more informative warning for your situation than you originally saw for the CFA.  Did you originally get standard errors with the CFA, which you don't get now?  If you can provide more information about the versions of R and lavaan you were using before and currently, Yves might be able to comment about specific changes (especially if you can provide him some data that will reproduce the problem).  

Terry
